title: SongForge Capacity Thesis
description: Issue #18 AC4: the shape proof for PRD #6 / decision #8 -- sse_connected_listeners rises with the number of connected clients while radio_advances_total and datastore-op counters stay flat, because SSE fan-out is in-process off ONE Redis pub/sub subscription per app instance. Also charts write-path create-rate throughput (AC4b).

panels.title: Connected listeners + fan-out (both EXPECTED TO RISE)
panels.description: songforge_sse_connected_listeners (the value loadtest/connection-ceiling.js drives up) and rate(songforge_radio_pointer_events_relayed_total[1m]). Both rise together during a ramp: the relay counter increments once per listener per push, so it IS the in-process fan-out work -- it belongs on the 'rises' side, not the flat side. The thesis is that these climb while the datastore panels below stay flat.

panels.title: Radio advance + pointer PUBLISH rate (expected FLAT)
panels.description: rate(songforge_radio_advances_total[1m]) and rate(songforge_radio_pointer_events_published_total[1m]) -- the thesis's direct observable: these stay flat regardless of listener count, because only ONE leader drives the clock-triggered advance and publishes each pointer change ONCE to Redis. (The per-listener relay counter is deliberately NOT here -- it grows with listeners and lives on the 'rises' panel to the left.)

panels.title: Datastore-op rate (expected FLAT as listener count rises)
panels.description: ACTUAL datastore operations from the exporters -- Postgres transactions (pg_stat_database_xact_commit + xact_rollback) and Redis commands (redis_commands_processed_total). These, not HTTP request volume, are the datastore-facing work that must NOT scale with sse_connected_listeners: a listener holds an in-process SSE connection and never issues a per-tick datastore read/write. (HTTP request rate would rise here just from new /events connections + /metrics scrapes, so it can't establish datastore-independence -- it lives on the Service RED dashboard instead.)

panels.title: Create-rate throughput (write path, AC4b)
panels.description: rate(songforge_jobs_created_total[1m]) vs rate(songforge_jobs_dispatched_total[1m]) -- driven by loadtest/create-rate.js against the simulator seam. The two tracking each other shows the write path sustaining the target create-rate without the queue unboundedly backing up.
